scenes.headline: Working with Parquet
scenes.subtitle: The columnar format built for analytics.
scenes.narration: Parquet is a compressed, columnar file format that is the default choice for analytics in Spark.

scenes.headline: Why Parquet wins
items: Columnar layout reads only the columns you need
The schema is stored inside the file
scenes.narration: Parquet's columnar layout reads only the columns you need, and built-in compression shrinks storage. The schema is stored inside the file, and predicate pushdown lets Spark skip data that a filter cannot match.

scenes.headline: Round-tripping Parquet
scenes.narration: We read a Parquet dataset, then filter it to a single year and write the result back as Parquet. Because Parquet supports predicate pushdown, Spark can skip files and column chunks that the year filter rules out, reading far less data.

scenes.headline: Parquet vs CSV
scenes.narration: Parquet is columnar, compressed, and carries its own schema, making it fast and pushdown-friendly. CSV is simple row-based text with an inferred schema, but it is slow and bulky at scale.

scenes.text: Default to Parquet for storage — it reads faster and costs less than text formats.
scenes.narration: Make Parquet your default storage format, because it reads faster and costs less than plain text formats like CSV.
